budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager thanked the legislative delegation for securing regional funding for fire and EMS services after the Nashoba Valley Medical Center closure, but said the town would not rely on it for ongoing operations since distribution details are unknown.
The town manager reported Lunenburg Public Schools is receiving a state cyber grant to upgrade three end-of-support network switches.
The town manager reported the final FY26 Chapter 90 apportionment came in well above what was assumed at town meeting, leaving additional funds available for road work.
The town manager relayed rough cost estimates for continuing with the current design firm on Town Hall/Ritter plus Brooks House, versus starting over with a new firm.
The town received one bid for the court resurfacing project that came in under the budgeted amount and is finalizing a contract.

budget_items.topic: Town meeting warrant postcard mailing cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member estimated the cost of mailing a full warrant booklet to every registered voter, part of the case for switching to a postcard notice.
A board member noted the state provided additional Chapter 70 funding and suggested coordinating with the school department on a warrant article to appropriate it.

budget_items.topic: Clean Water SRF grant - asset management inventory
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager described a stormwater asset-mapping project mostly funded by a state grant with the remainder from town funds, requiring board authorization to file the application.
The board accepted a monetary gift from the Lunenburg Friendly Seniors to the Council on Aging.
Two accounts payable warrants were presented to the board without discussion.
The board of assessors liaison reported FY26 growth in assessed value and noted personal property assessed values were lower than the prior year.
The principal assessor cited declining abatement counts as evidence of improved assessing practices compared to the volume issued during the fiscal 2023 lakefront valuation crisis.

decisions.decision: Board agreed in principle to move to a postcard-format town meeting warrant notice with hard copies available on request, and directed that drafting begin; a formal vote will follow when finalized.
Board directed that any warrant article moving additional Chapter 70 state funding to the schools be drafted as an additional appropriation article, with communication to the school department first.

Board declined to commit further resources to researching a BYOB policy change at this time, but was open to the town manager informally asking the requesting business about pursuing a wine/malt pouring license instead.

Board decided not to vote to accept the tax investigation report as submitted and to remove it from the agenda, since none of the current members were involved in the original investigation and the board of assessors has its own corrections pending.
Confirmed a quorum is expected for the August 26 tri-board meeting.
Identified that the board will lack a quorum for the week of September 16 due to two members' absences and will work around it.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Select Board ratified a new police lieutenant and several other appointments, heard a lengthy update from the assessor's office on reforms since the 2023 lakefront tax crisis, and set the fall Special Town Meeting for November 18, 2025 with its warrant timeline. The board also worked through a list of possible warrant articles, declined to pursue a BYOB alcohol policy change for now, authorized a stormwater grant application, sent a legislative support letter for the Nashoba Associated Boards of Health pension issue, and chose not to vote on accepting an unfinished prior tax investigation report.

what_happened.line: Select Board set a fall Special Town Meeting for Nov. 18, 2025, with the warrant opening Aug. 20 and closing Oct. 2.
Board declined to vote on accepting a prior tax investigation report and pulled it from the agenda, since no current member took part in the original inquiry.
Board ratified the town manager's appointment of Shawn Zarate to police lieutenant.
Board declined to commit further staff time to a BYOB alcohol policy change for now.
Board authorized filing for a state stormwater grant to fund asset-mapping work.

why_it_matters: Residents will have until Oct. 2 to see what lands on the Nov. 18 Special Town Meeting warrant, including a possible article moving added Chapter 70 school funding.
Setting aside the unfinished tax investigation report leaves open questions about the 2023 lakefront valuation episode, even as the assessor's office described reforms since then.
The stormwater grant, if awarded, would shift part of the cost of a required asset-management inventory onto state rather than town funds.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on every vote's substance and outcome — all ten non-procedural motions passed unanimously in both — but ours mishears five proper names/places (Zrate, Beardmore/Dupre, Leger, Cajka, Passios) and drops or garbles several digits in warrant and apportionment figures. The one thing a reader should check: ours lists a "Liz" as a Select Board member present, but the official minutes name only four members present (Nuzzolo, Emkey, McLeod, Lehtinen) with Vice-Chair Amanda Moore absent — no "Liz" appears at all, and two of ours's dollar figures for municipal building design ($80,000/$40,000) don't match either of the official's two figures ($120,000/$210,000).
